reasoning: Defect is real and correctly characterized. numbduck/ducklib.py:237 has signatures["duckdb_vector_get_validity"] = uint64(intp), wrapped at ducklib.py:1207-1210. duckdb.h confirms the C prototype is `DUCKDB_C_API uint64_t *duckdb_vector_get_validity(duckdb_vector vector)` -- it returns a pointer (uint64_t*), not a scalar count. numbduck/CLAUDE.md:97 documents the project-wide convention that '@cfunc signatures must use nb_types.intp (not nb_types.voidptr) because numbduck uses intp for all pointers', and the sibling pointer-returning accessor duckdb_vector_get_data is correctly typed intp(intp) at ducklib.py:236. duckdb_validity_row_is_valid (ducklib.py:234, int8(intp, intp)) expects its validity-mask argument as intp, matching the C signature `bool duckdb_validity_row_is_valid(uint64_t *validity, idx_t row)`. Empirical confirmation: test/test_ducklib.py:1117-1118, inside the @njit-compiled jit_prepare_bind_execute function, must write `duckdb_validity_row_is_valid(intp(v3_validity_p), intp(0))` -- an explicit intp(...) cast on the validity pointer -- whereas the intp-returning duckdb_vector_get_data results (v0_p/v1_p/v2_p, same file, lines ~1097-1110) are used directly with no such cast. This intp(...) cast is a singular outlier in the test file (only occurrence of an explicit intp() wrap around a proxy return value before feeding it to another proxy call), consistent with numba's fixed-signature njit/cfunc call resolution not silently unifying uint64 and intp (a numba TypingError without the cast), not just a stylistic choice. So the claim holds: this is the only pointer-returning proxy signature typed uint64 instead of intp, it is a genuine contract violation, and it is independently reproduced by the test suite needing a workaround cast. However, the severity is better characterized as low rather than medium: per the finding's own impact analysis, the bit pattern is identical on the supported LP64 platform (uint64 and intp are both 64-bit), no wrong result or memory corruption occurs, and a missing cast fails loudly at numba compile time (TypingError) rather than silently misbehaving -- this is a type-hygiene/convention-consistency defect with an easy, well-contained fix, not a functional-correctness bug. This matches the severity the prior 2026-06-29 review gave to the same/related findings (DCK-sig-COR-2, DCK-wrap-COR-2, and its own XC-numbox-COR-1, all rated 'low' for this exact ducklib.py:236/237 issue).
